title: The Tide of the Old Mill House
premise: Xanthe Eastwick, a ghostwriter who has built a career on erasing himself, returns to the coastal village of Porthollow to ghostwrite the memoirs of celebrated novelist Caspian Vane—only to discover that the memoir's central mystery is a letter Xanthe himself wrote eleven years ago and never sent, addressed to Merrin Tallow, the mill keeper's daughter he abandoned. As the village prepares for its autumn tide festival, the letter resurfaces in Caspian's possession, and Xanthe must decide whether to keep ghosting his own life or claim it. When Caspian threatens to publish the letter as fiction under his own name, Xanthe confronts him publicly at the festival, confesses authorship—and his love—to Merrin before the whole village. The novel ends with Xanthe signing his first book under his own name, staying in Porthollow, and forgiving the man in the mirror.
about_author: Juniper Lockridge is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who spent a decade writing other people's love stories before daring to write her own. She lives on the Cornish coast, where she collects unsent letters and repairs old clocks.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Xanthe arrives in Porthollow under contract to ghostwrite Caspian Vane's memoirs, telling himself the heart is a trainable muscle. He checks into the inn above the old mill house and glimpses Merrin Tallow across the courtyard, feeling the first crack in his discipline. Emotional beat: guarded denial, the ache of homecoming disguised as business.

chapters.title: Salt and Second Chances
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. A storm strands Xanthe and Merrin together repairing the mill's floodgate; their easy intimacy terrifies him more than the rising water. He learns she never left Porthollow, never married, and still keeps the mill running alone. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness, the past pressing close through small familiar gestures.

chapters.title: The Memoir of Another Man
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Interviewing Caspian, Xanthe realizes with horror that the novelist's 'great lost romance' chapter mirrors his own history—the mill house, the festival, a girl named M. Caspian hints he possesses a letter proving it all. Emotional beat: dread and possessiveness, watching his stolen life become another man's material.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: POV: Merrin. Merrin finds an unopened envelope wedged in the mill's stone foundation, postmarked eleven years ago, addressed in handwriting she'd know anywhere. She doesn't open it yet; instead she watches Xanthe at the harbor and wonders why he flinches when she mentions the festival. Emotional beat: quiet hope shadowed by old betrayal.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Caspian reveals the letter—he bought it years ago from a junk dealer—and proposes publishing it as his own fictional confession, cementing his legend. Xanthe, bound by contract and shame, almost agrees. That night he drafts a confession to Merrin and burns it. Emotional beat: self-loathing crystallizing into a decision he can't yet make.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unsent Things
chapters.summary: POV: Merrin. Merrin finally reads the letter: a young Xanthe's promise to return after one winter away, and his fear that he was never worth waiting for. She confronts him at the mill; he lies badly, claiming the letter is a forgery for Caspian's book. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharpening into fury, love refusing to die quietly.

chapters.title: Contract Terms
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Xanthe discovers Caspian has scheduled the 'letter reveal' as the climax of his festival keynote—a public theft of Xanthe's one true thing. His editor warns that breaking the NDA will end his career. Alone, he finally faces the mirror and admits the person he most needs forgiveness from is himself. Emotional beat: the turning point, cowardice examined and rejected.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: POV: Merrin. On festival eve, a spring tide floods the mill and Merrin is trapped salvaging her father's ledger books. Xanthe arrives without being called, wades in, and they fight the water side by side until dawn. Soaked and laughing and crying, they stop pretending. Emotional beat: catharsis through shared labor, walls down at last.

chapters.title: The Keynote
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. At the festival, Caspian begins reading the letter aloud as his own. Xanthe takes the stage, names himself as its author, and reads the ending aloud to Merrin in front of the village—an apology eleven years late. Caspian's fraud collapses as witnesses confirm the handwriting. Emotional beat: public vulnerability, the climax of claimed identity.

chapters.title: Signed, At Last
chapters.summary: POV: Merrin, closing with Xanthe. Weeks later, Xanthe has torn up the contract, paid the penalty, and finished a short book of his own under his own name; Merrin sets the type on the mill's old press. They hang the first printed page where the letter was found. Emotional beat: belonging earned, inheritance reclaimed—not of property, but of self.
